sn10.4:1.1: Maṇimālika means “garland of jewels”, Maṇibhadda means “lucky jewel”. _Yakkhas_ of that name are found in both Brahmanism and Jainism as bestowers of wealth. Hindu texts identify him as brother of Kuvera, king of _yakkhas_, and tutellary deity of merchants and travellers. Mahāvīra was once said to have stayed at a Maṇibhadra shrine, but that was in Mithila, north of the Ganges.
